objective: Bind every VerificationResult evidence_refs list to the entity evidence that supports the actual verification outcome, fail closed when claimed-object evidence is missing, and deterministically deduplicate references without changing schemas or public verifier signatures.
decision_supported: Whether a World Model verification outcome is supported by evidence bound to the entities participating in that outcome.
acceptance: verify_object_in_tray returns confirmed only when the claimed object has non-empty entity-bound evidence.

An observed object relation without claimed-object evidence returns insufficient_evidence with reason_code evidence_missing and recovery_hint re_observe even when unrelated global or entity evidence is abundant.
Confirmed object verification returns only the claimed object's entity-bound evidence and excludes state-level and unrelated-entity evidence.
Kit, inspection, workspace-clearance, parcel-sorting, and parcel-policy verification results derive evidence_refs only from entities supporting the selected outcome.
Refuted results retain evidence bound to the entities that establish the refutation and exclude unrelated evidence.
When no supporting entity-bound reference exists, evidence_refs contains only system://world-state/no-evidence to preserve the non-empty VerificationResult contract.
Supporting entity IDs are traversed in lexicographic order, references retain their stored per-entity order, and duplicate references retain only their first deterministic occurrence.
Adversarial states with abundant evidence for wrong entities cannot confirm a claim or contaminate returned evidence_refs.

Existing verifier function signatures, claim formats, rule versions, status semantics, and reason-code precedence remain unchanged except for the specified fail-closed missing-object-evidence behavior.
No JSON Schema, Python contract model, reducer, event store, integration consumer, demo, backend, robot, firmware, simulation, or deployment file is modified.
evidence: Before implementation, each newly added Issue #50 test fails because unrelated evidence is accepted, unrelated evidence is returned, or duplicate support references are not scoped deterministically.
After implementation, the five named Issue #50 tests pass and directly execute every verifier evidence-selection path added or changed by this issue.
The complete tests/unit/test_world_model.py output passes and preserves existing verifier status, reason-code, validation, reducer, parcel-sorting, and parcel-policy behavior.
Assertions compare exact VerificationResult.status, reason_code, recovery_hint, and evidence_refs values for confirmed, refuted, and insufficient-evidence outcomes.
Adversarial test output proves global evidence and evidence bound only to wrong entities neither confirms the claim nor appears in returned evidence_refs.
Determinism assertions compare exact evidence_refs lists across repeated references and different entity-map insertion orders.
Task Packet validation with --base main proves every Git-visible changed path is inside one approved allowed_paths set.
make check output proves lint, formatting, full tests, contract validation, scenario validation, golden-set validation, context validation, and scripted/offline demos pass.
stop_conditions: Any required implementation or test change falls outside the three allowed_paths.
Completing the issue requires changing interfaces, JSON Schema, libs/contracts, WorldState, reducer, event store, or public package exports.
Completing the issue requires changes in Backend, Agent Runtime, Perception, Motion, robot, firmware, simulation, deployment, demo, or integration-test code.
A relation-level evidence field or another public contract change is required to determine the supporting evidence set.
A complex refuted outcome cannot be mapped to supporting entity IDs from the existing WorldState representation without inventing new semantics.
A verifier public function signature, claim format, rule version, or unrelated status and reason-code precedence must change.
A newly added test fails before implementation for a reason other than the current global or unrelated evidence behavior.
An existing test or public gate fails for a reason unrelated to Issue #50.
Task Packet validation reports a path outside allowed_paths.
The change affects physical completion, safety policy, robot control, firmware, or another protected boundary.
data_classification: Repository-local synthetic World Model test data only.
model_policy: Deterministic local Python logic only; no model inference or network access.
risks_and_fallbacks: VerificationResult evidence_refs will become narrower; callers that incorrectly relied on unrelated run-wide evidence must be treated as defective consumers rather than preserved.

The existing internal WorldState Python representation differs structurally from the public WorldState JSON Schema; this issue does not resolve that drift because entity_evidence_refs already supplies the required internal binding.
If exact refutation support cannot be represented with current entity_evidence_refs, stop and request a separate interface-scoped design instead of modifying schemas in Issue #50.
Rollback is a revert of the verifier and unit-test changes; do not retain a partial implementation that mixes scoped and global evidence selection.
